notes:
Written by ea-07 on 2026-10-25 from six pages (the budget was 2-5; the Jianzhou page is thin, so the unification, Nurhaci, Hulun and Ming-Manchuria pages carry the dates). The Jianzhou Jurchens are a tribal state Cliopatria lacks: the four keyframes are new and no Cliopatria shape is reviewed. The ming-dynasty dossier records the Ming vassalage over this slug in 1403-1618; Cliopatria's Ming shapes include Liaodong, which the Jianzhou country adjoins.

Drawn from the pages: dates (1403 guard, 1587 Fe Ala, 1591 Fushun-to-Yalu, 1601 Hada, 1603 Hetu Ala, 1607 Hoifa, 1613 Ula, 1616 Jin), the markets at Kaiyuan and Fushun, the 'five tribes' north of the Yalu. Read, not drawn by a page: every shape. The Hetu Ala disc (124.8 E, 41.7 N, 80 km, the same stand-in as later-jin-dynasty) and the Benxi and Dandong discs stand for 'from Fushun to the Yalu River'; Fushun stays Ming land to 1618. The Hada disc is at Tieling (the Guangshun Pass is east of Kaiyuan, which the gazetteer lacks); the Ula and Hoifa discs are in Jilin city's neighbourhood, the same reading as later-jin-dynasty, with no page behind the places.

Disagreements: the Jianzhou page has the Ming commander at Fushun killed in 1473, the unification page has Wang Gao killing one there in 1573 and executed in 1575; the Hada fall in 1601 (Haixi, Hulun, unification pages) or 1603 (Nurhaci page, after an attack in 1599); the Hoifa in 1607 on every page. Not settled: the Jianzhou Left and Right guards' location before 1583 (the Odoli, Huligai and Tuowen tribes are named without places), the dates of the Wild Jurchen conquest (1611, no place; not drawn), the end of Ming vassalage in 1618 (see the Ming ledger), and the beginning of Nurhaci's own state before 1616. The state ends in 1616; the Later Jin dossier carries 1616 onward.

Counterparts: 'nobody' for the 1591 corridor; 'haixi-jurchens' for the Hulun gains; 'ming-dynasty' on the founding guard; 'later-jin-dynasty' on the dissolve.
